extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders, commenters, regulated entities, and legal practitioners concerned with EPA's Endangerment and Cause or Contribute Findings under CAA section 202(a)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal/technical criteria for making and defending EPA's determination that greenhouse gas emissions from new motor vehicles 'endanger' public health or welfare and 'cause or contribute' to air pollution under Clean Air Act §202(a), including procedural requirements for notice-and-comment and responses to public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endangerment finding must be based on scientific considerations, not policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory question is whether sufficient information exists to make an endangerment finding; policy reasons do not justify avoiding or delaying the finding if the science is sufficiently certain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Massachusetts v. EPA: EPA can avoid action only if it determines greenhouse gases do not contribute to climate change or provides a reasonable explanation why it cannot/will not exercise discretion. Commenters' policy-based reasons for delay are rejected; the Court interpreted the statute to limit consideration essentially to science for the endangerment determination (quoting language at 549 U.S. 533-34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator may define the pollutant as the aggregate group of well-mixed greenhouse gases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator defines the air pollutant that contributes to climate change as the aggregate group of the well-mixed greenhouse gases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is based on shared attributes: sufficiently long-lived to be well mixed globally, directly emitted, exert a climate warming effect by trapping outgoing infrared heat, and being the focus of climate change science and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution finding supported by quantitative emissions comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine if emissions from CAA §202(a) source categories contribute to air pollution that endangers health/welfare, EPA compared emissions from those categories to total global and total U.S. greenhouse gas emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings noted that section 202(a) source categories account for ~4% of global and just over 23% of U.S. well-mixed GHG emissions; comparisons showing U.S. motor-vehicle emissions are larger than every other individual nation except China, Russia, and India support that motor-vehicle emissions make a meaningful contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endangerment finding considers present and future risks and increasing severity over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that adverse effects (e.g., wildfires, pests, disease) and climate change impacts increase over time supports a finding that greenhouse gas pollution endangers public welfare of current and future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA emphasizes that risks and severity of adverse impacts are expected to increase over time and that support for a positive endangerment finding strengthens when considering expected future conditions where temperatures continue to rise.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may issue endangerment/contribution findings separately from emissions standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA §202(a) does not require that endangerment/contribution findings and emissions standards be proposed or finalized together; the statute is silent on timing and EPA has procedural discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 202(a) envisions two separate actions: (1) determination on contribution/endangerment, and (2) a separate decision on issuing appropriate emissions standards. Issuing the findings separately does not violate the statute and is within EPA's discretion; commenters' arguments that separate action deprives them of the ability to comment on implications were rejected because the two actions address different issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA has discretion to group classes/categories together or separately for findings
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may consider classes or categories of new motor vehicles separately or together when making contribution and endangerment determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute does not limit EPA to issuing an endangerment finding only when ready to issue standards for every class/category; restricting grouping would remove discretion CAA §202(a) provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment period adequacy standard (60-day rulemaking period and prior ANPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 60-day public comment period on the Proposed Findings satisfied procedural requirements (CAA §307 requires 30 days and 30 days after hearings) and was adequate especially given prior release of information in a 120-day ANPR and accompanying TSD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA relied on prior ANPR (120-day comment period) and TSDs; overlapping climate-related proceedings do not by themselves render the comment period insufficient. Requests to extend must show concrete need; EPA concluded the official period provided meaningful opportunity to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA need only respond to significant arguments, not every comment individually
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the very large number of comments, EPA summarized and provided responses to each significant argument, assertion and question rather than responding individually to each comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses to significant issues are contained in the multi-volume Response to Comments document, organized by subject area; mass-mail comments are summarized with representative copies posted in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of mass mail/comment campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass mail campaigns (groups of comments identical or very similar) are handled by posting a representative copy of the comment in the public docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes that roughly two-thirds of mass-mail comments supported the Findings; representative copies are posted in Docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2009-0171 at regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to reopen/extend comment period require showing of material impact from new information
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to reopen the comment period based on new information (e.g., alleged destruction of raw temperature data) must demonstrate that the new information would materially affect trends or conclusions relied upon in the TSD/assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed the allegation regarding HadCRUT raw data and found other independent temperature records (NOAA, NASA) and extensive peer review produce essentially the same long-term trends; the commenter did not show the absence of raw data would materially alter conclusions, so reopening was unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor procedural or typographical errors do not invalidate notice if not a meaningful impediment
rubrics_metrics.description: A minor error in the Federal Register (e.g., an auto-corrected dash in an e-mail address) does not make notice defective if correct contact information was available elsewhere and the public had alternative avenues to submit comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA documented that the e-mail address was correct in the signature version on EPA's website and in submission instructions, and that over 190,000 emails had been received to date; other submission means (regulations.gov, mail, fax) were available.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may rely on established scientific assessments and technical support documents (TSD)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Findings can be informed by and rely upon the major scientific assessments and the technical support document that summarize the scientific state-of-knowledge used to justify endangerment and contribution determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA referenced the TSD accompanying the action and prior major assessments (IPCC, CCSP, NOAA, NASA) that had undergone public review; the ANPR and TSD previously released provided ample time for review and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential support or stakeholder announcements do not by themselves preordain rulemaking outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Public statements of support by the President or stakeholders for the agency's plan to conduct notice-and-comment rulemaking do not equate to a preordained final decision or prejudgment of the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explained that announcements described a plan to initiate a notice-and-comment process and did not announce a final rule; stakeholders reserved rights to participate fully in the process.
